Surgical · Autologous fat transfer

Fat Transfer Breast Augmentation: What to Know

Fat transfer breast augmentation removes fat from a donor area using liposuction, processes it, and transfers selected fat to the breasts. It may suit certain patients seeking a relatively modest increase in volume without implants.

Home/Surgical/Fat transfer

The amount of fat that can be transferred safely, and the proportion that remains over time, vary. Some transferred fat may not survive, and more than one procedure may be needed to approach a patient’s goals.

Fat transfer data from the American Society of Plastic Surgeons

ASPS describes fat transfer breast augmentation as using liposuction to remove fat from another part of the body and inject it into the breasts, and notes that it is best suited to patients who want a relatively small increase with a natural result. The ASPS average surgeon fee for breast augmentation with fat grafting is $5,719 (United States, surgeon’s fee only). ASPS also refers to the technique as breast augmentation with fat grafting, and cites research into mega-volume fat transfer with pre-expansion and into techniques intended to double breast size using the patient’s own fat.

Fat transfer FAQs

Some transferred fat can survive long term, but a proportion may be reabsorbed. The final result varies between individuals, and additional procedures may be considered.

The safe volume and the amount that survives vary individually, so fat transfer is generally associated with a more modest, individualised increase than implant-based augmentation.
